title: Homeowner's Identity Exposure During Registration
description: Homeowner's personal identity information (name, contact details, biometric data) is exposed during account registration and camera/sensor enrollment, potentially enabling identity theft or unauthorized profiling.
assumptions: Homeowner provides personal identifying information during registration process

title: Unauthorized Data Disclosure at Registration
description: Homeowner's sensitive data (including camera/sensor configuration and usage patterns) may be disclosed to unauthorized parties during the registration and enrollment process.
assumptions: Registration process may lack adequate access controls or encryption

title: Meta-data Exposure During Data Transmission
description: Meta-data about the parties (homeowner and home hub) in transit may be used to link or identify the homeowner, potentially enabling tracking or profiling across multiple devices.
assumptions: Data flows may contain identifying meta-data about the parties involved

title: Homeowner Identification at Home Hub
description: Home Hub may identify and track the homeowner through registration data, potentially enabling persistent profiling and unauthorized surveillance of home activities.
assumptions: Home Hub stores and processes homeowner identification data

title: Insecure Data Storage at Home Hub
description: Homeowner's personal data and camera/sensor information may be stored insecurely at the Home Hub, increasing risk of unauthorized access or data breaches.
assumptions: Home Hub may lack adequate security controls for data storage

title: Access Code Interception
description: The temporary access code transmitted from Guest User (EE2) to Home Hub (P1) could be intercepted by third parties during data in transit, potentially allowing unauthorized access to the front door.

title: Guest Identity Learning
description: The act of entering an access code at the Home Hub causes the system to learn about the guest's identity or access patterns, potentially enabling profiling or tracking of guest movements.

title: Guest Presence Detection
description: The Home Hub's processing of the access code entry may reveal the guest's presence through system responses, side effects, or communication patterns that could be observed by others.

title: Access Code Deception
description: The Home Hub may be deceived about the validity of the access code or the guest's identity if the code is forged or if the system fails to properly verify the code.

title: Access Authorization Non-repudiation
description: The guest may not be able to prove they authorized the access code entry, as the system may not maintain verifiable records of the guest's actions.

title: Lawful basis for data collection
description: Home Hub may collect motion/door/sensor events without a clear lawful basis under applicable privacy laws (e.g., GDPR Art. 6). Users may not be aware of the legal grounds for this data collection.
assumptions: Assumes the Home Hub collects data without explicit consent or other lawful basis.

title: Lack of notice about data collection
description: Users may not be adequately informed about what motion/door/sensor events are being collected, how they are used, and who they are shared with.
assumptions: Assumes minimal or no privacy notice is provided to users about the data collection activities.

title: Excessive data collection
description: Home Hub may collect more motion/door/sensor data than necessary for the stated purpose, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Assumes the Home Hub collects all available sensor data without filtering or limiting collection to what's strictly necessary.

title: Data integrity during transmission
description: Motion/door/sensor events in transit from Home Hub to Local Event Log could be intercepted, tampered with, or corrupted, potentially leading to inaccurate records.
assumptions: Assumes data flows over a network without adequate encryption or integrity checks.

title: Data integrity at storage
description: Stored motion/door/sensor events in Local Event Log could be corrupted, tampered with, or lost, compromising the accuracy and reliability of the records.
assumptions: Assumes the Local Event Log lacks adequate backup, integrity checks, or access controls.

title: Unintended consequences from data storage
description: Stored motion/door/sensor events could be accessed by unauthorized parties or used for purposes beyond the original intent, potentially leading to privacy violations or security risks.
assumptions: Assumes the Local Event Log may have inadequate access controls or could be compromised.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of camera data at source
description: Home Hub may disclose recorded camera clips to unauthorized parties through improper access controls or compromised credentials before upload to cloud storage.
assumptions: Assumes Home Hub has appropriate access controls and authentication mechanisms in place.

title: Unintended data upload from source
description: Home Hub may upload camera data unintentionally due to user error, system malfunction, or unauthorized access to the upload mechanism.
assumptions: Assumes Home Hub has proper user authentication and error handling mechanisms.

title: Data interception during transmission
description: Camera clips in transit from Home Hub to Cloud Video Storage may be intercepted by unauthorized parties through network sniffing or man-in-the-middle attacks.
assumptions: Assumes data is transmitted over potentially unencrypted or partially encrypted network connections.

title: Metadata identification through flow
description: Flow metadata (timestamps, packet sizes, source/destination addresses) may be used to link and identify users or their activities.
assumptions: Assumes metadata is not adequately protected or anonymized during transmission.

title: Unauthorized disclosure at destination
description: Cloud Video Storage may disclose recorded camera clips to unauthorized parties through improper access controls, data breaches, or unauthorized sharing with third parties.
assumptions: Assumes Cloud Video Storage has appropriate access controls and security measures in place.

title: Unintended data processing at destination
description: Cloud Video Storage may process camera data unintentionally (e.g., for analytics, advertising, or other purposes) without user consent.
assumptions: Assumes Cloud Video Storage has clear policies on data usage and user consent mechanisms.

title: Unintended data disclosure to third party
description: Home Hub shares real-time motion alert data with Mobile App Backend (P2), which is a third party not directly involved in the motion detection process. This explicit disclosure of personal data to an external party may violate privacy expectations.
assumptions: Motion alert contains personal data about home occupancy and activity patterns

title: Data broadcast through data flow
description: Real-time motion alert data is transmitted across the data flow boundary, potentially exposing personal data to interception or unauthorized access during transit. The flow itself acts as a conduit for personal data disclosure.
assumptions: Data in transit may be intercepted or exposed to unauthorized parties

title: Data disclosure at destination
description: Mobile App Backend receives and processes motion alert data, potentially storing or further sharing this personal data with other systems or third parties without explicit consent.
assumptions: Mobile App Backend may have broader data usage policies than intended

title: Location data exposure through motion notifications
description: The mobile app backend shares motion-detected location data with the homeowner, potentially revealing the homeowner's location patterns and movement habits.
assumptions: Motion detection is tied to geographic location

title: Homeowner identification through notification
description: The motion-detected notification could be used to identify the specific homeowner, potentially enabling tracking of individual household members.
assumptions: Notification is associated with a specific homeowner account

title: Unintended disclosure of notification metadata
description: Data in transit may contain metadata about the parties (homeowner and app backend) that could be used to link or identify them, potentially revealing communication patterns.
assumptions: Network metadata is captured by third parties

title: Location tracking through notification timing
description: The homeowner receives motion-detected notifications that could be used to track their location patterns and movement habits over time.
assumptions: Notification timing correlates with actual location

title: Unintended disclosure of personal activity patterns
description: The homeowner may receive notifications that reveal more personal activity information than intended, potentially exposing sensitive behavioral patterns.
assumptions: Motion detection captures all movement types

title: Linkability of Aggregated Device-Usage Data
description: Even though data is aggregated, metadata or correlation with other data sources could enable re-identification of individual users.
assumptions: Aggregation may not be sufficient to prevent re-identification through cross-referencing with other datasets.

title: Intrusiveness of Device-Usage Data Sharing
description: Sharing device-usage analytics represents an intrusion into user privacy by collecting and transmitting behavioral data about device usage patterns.
assumptions: Device-usage data includes behavioral patterns that could be sensitive or revealing about user habits.

title: Non-Compliance with Privacy Regulations
description: Sharing device-usage analytics may violate privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA) if consent mechanisms or data minimization principles are not properly implemented.
assumptions: The sharing process may not have adequate consent or data minimization controls.

title: Linkability via Flow Metadata
description: Metadata about the data flow (parties involved, timing, volume) could be used to link or identify the source and destination entities.
assumptions: Flow metadata is transmitted and could be analyzed by third parties.

title: Unintended Data Exposure During Transit
description: Data in transit could be intercepted by unauthorized parties, leading to unintended exposure of device-usage analytics.
assumptions: Data transmission may not be adequately protected against interception.

title: Linkability at Destination
description: The cloud analytics vendor could link the received data with other data sources to re-identify users or create profiles.
assumptions: The vendor has access to additional data sources for correlation.

title: Intrusive Data Processing at Destination
description: The vendor may process the data in ways that are more intrusive than originally intended, such as creating detailed user profiles or selling the data.
assumptions: The vendor has broad discretion in how to use the received data.

title: Non-Compliance by Destination Entity
description: The cloud analytics vendor may not comply with applicable privacy regulations when processing the received data.
assumptions: The vendor may have inadequate privacy controls or may operate in jurisdictions with weaker protections.

title: Excessive data retrieval
description: Mobile app backend may retrieve more video data than necessary for playback, violating data minimization principle.
assumptions: Assumes the process retrieves the full video clip rather than only necessary segments.

title: Insufficient data confidentiality
description: Retrieved video may be displayed or processed without adequate confidentiality controls, potentially exposing sensitive content to unauthorized viewing.
assumptions: Assumes the process handles video playback without proper access controls.

title: Data integrity risk during processing
description: Video data may be modified or corrupted during processing at the mobile app backend, compromising data integrity.
assumptions: Assumes the process may introduce modifications to the video data.

title: Data in transit confidentiality
description: Video data transmitted between cloud storage and mobile app backend may be intercepted or exposed during transit.
assumptions: Assumes the data flow may not be adequately encrypted.
